status: Uncommitted working study. Local review scope is recorded below.

common_inputs.material: One orienting face of each mirror mouth. Seven cuts in order of 0 through 6 encounters, driven, static material preparation with incoming spin up and radial pin eta*n. Per-event excited survival cos(sqrt(2)*0.33)^2. The rim is the innermost cut. Radius 16 for matching the exterior is a model input in lattice units. Holding the material fixed excludes backreaction and cannot establish formation or lifetime.
common_inputs.field: All finite-model link phases are free. Each angular triangle and radial quadrilateral has four equal spring elements in series, W(F)=8K sin^2(F/8) on the principal branch. This is an assumed four-element loop response even for a triangular face. Face orientations are fixed globally. An energetic tie costs W(pi). A nonzero prism index costs >=5W(2pi/5) by convexity; in the absence of any cell charge or tie the integer is the same on all cuts. Nonzero flux on seven cuts costs at least 7N_f W(2pi/N_f) plus the exterior monopole cost.
common_inputs.exterior: The exterior is positive and source-free beyond Rb=16, with field coefficient 1 when K=1. The angular finite-volume graph has mass M of triangular solid angles and stiffness L given by primal/dual geodesic length weights. If M^(-1/2) L M^(-1/2) has eigenvector matrix U and eigenvalues l(l+1), the energy is F^T M^(-1/2) U diag(1/(l+1)) U^T M^(-1/2) F/(2Rb). This follows by minimizing each radial harmonic with the given boundary flux. A flux 2pi*n costs >=pi*n^2/(2Rb); the radial continuation costs at most sum(F_f^2/Omega_f)/(2Rb) at the optimum. The certificate bounds energy on each side of a principal-phase tie. The weak case excludes all ties. The strong case excludes outer ties, which are the ones that affect the exterior quadratic form. The calculation assumes no further compact defects beyond Rb; it does not predict propagation in an unconstrained bulk.
common_inputs.selective_contact: For endpoint Bloch lengths p_i and dominant unit spinors z_i, the edge energy is G*sqrt(p_i*p_j)*(|z_i^dag z_j|-Re[exp(-ia_ij) z_i^dag z_j]). At zero polarization take the edge energy to be zero independent of spinor. This models two coherent arms in which the fraction p_i follows the dominant spinor with the rest incoherent. A selective subpopulation and shared phase registration are new material assumptions. A common site rephasing also shifts the physical link registration. The dimensionless feed coefficient g=Gfeed/K and rim G=64K are held across mirror comparisons. Measurement: calibrate phase and both torque quadratures on held neighboring sites, including at vanishing polarization, relative to a measured spring energy K.
common_inputs.selective_certificate: The through-going trial copies rim phases to every cut in a shared meridional gauge. It pays zero radial slip and no rim attachment. The screened trial uses local preferred phases on every bond with flat outer shell and zero exterior energy. Wrong cut degree or a tie requires some triangular loop to exhaust b=pi-|F_preferred| of aggregate angular slip on its edges. This costs >=3G*w_min*(1-cos(b/3)) with w_min the smallest visibility on that triangle. In the weak region the through-going upper bound excludes any cell charge, tie or wrong rim degree. In the strong region the screened upper bound excludes wrong degrees or ties at both endpoints. Internal compensated pairs and metastable states are not classified by that comparison. The tabulated windows are sufficient across two finite lattices (128 and 512 triangles per sphere), two geometrical rotations, and both mirrors. They are not continuum thresholds.
common_inputs.passive_hopping: Each arm has the same incident spin. An emitted record specifies the ordered encounter number from entry and its Cartesian component, with common real intersite overlap u in [0,1] (realized by shared plus private record components). Histories are phase aligned with no added propagation phase. Let P_i project onto the pinned direction, Q_i=I-P_i and v_i=(P_i+r^(k_i/2)*Q_i)up. The link amplitude is v_i^dag v_j + u*(1-r^min(k_i,k_j))*(1+n_i dot n_j)*(Q_i up)^dag(Q_j up)/2. Adjacent nodes on the same radial lane give a positive real amplitude. On each face the complex product is bounded by the convex cone of its Bernstein coefficients in u. The all-preferred trial has zero attachment energy at any finite nonnegative edge strengths and zero outer flux. A bound below both the exterior monopole and the charged-prism/tie floor forces zero on every cut at a global minimum. Holding temperature, matter and drive fixed is part of this result; distinguishable records outside the tested family can change the local phase.
common_inputs.mobile_excitation: Test a separate Hamiltonian H_ii=-J p_i dot sigma, H_ij=-t exp(-i a_ij) I for positive t, zero temperature, positive J, and one mobile doublet, with no other rim attachment. The link phase on hopping is supplied. The physical origin and electric normalization of this internal angular connection are open. A separate measurement for each triangle allows an independent flux bias; those measurements do not define a joint energy for one shared carrier. At full six-state filling the loop energy is the trace. For a shared excitation anywhere on the rim, replacing each site's spinor by its norm bounds the lowest energy for every A from below by lambda_min(-t Adj-J diag|p|). A spinor Rayleigh trial at A=0 gives an upper bound for the neutral minimum. Outward-rounded interval arithmetic on a positive scalar comparison vector and this spinor bounds the possible matter-energy saving. t/K thresholds assume J/t fixed and the stated field cost in K units. Above these sufficient thresholds the outcome is open.
common_inputs.open: The earlier real trapped mode has no identified hopping bandwidth t or alignment J for this proposed doublet. The separate degenerate polarization extension allows different signed actions at the same stored energy and radial load. Deciding whether the rim actually supplies a selected subpopulation or enough occupied mobile modes requires an independent local spectrum, phase response and occupation law. No distant electromagnetic force, common charge unit across radii, or 0PN free acceleration is inferred.
